defects_found_in_revision_1.D1: P1b's tolerance would have made three absence claims vacuous. unexpected-credential-entry, project-key-ambiguous and foreign-session-state are all NAME-based, read from directory listings; an unenterable directory hides those names, so tolerating it would have reported the checks as passed without looking. Fixed: an unreadable regular FILE is recorded closed because its name is still visible in the parent listing; an unenterable DIRECTORY refuses with the registered code state-coverage-incomplete; an unreadable SELECTED file refuses specifically.
defects_found_in_revision_1.D2: P1a did not distinguish the turns and aimed a chmod at the manager-owned 0o660 restored working copy that accepted R1 established at 178875. It would have failed EPERM rather than corrupting it silently, since uid65532 cannot chmod a uid1000 file, but the intent was wrong. Fixed: P1a is turn-1 only and runtime-owned only, and ownership and type are verified through the same no-follow descriptor that is then fchmodded, so there is no check-to-change window.

established.blocking_objects: one runtime-owned directory 0o700 and three runtime-owned regular files 0o600, all gid1001
established.mechanism: setgid gave group ownership and never group permission bits -- the same distinction accepted R1 turned on at 178875, from the other side
established.observed_error: one opendir:EACCES; 11 entries, depth4, no bound reached; use-2/home absent

guarantees_preserved: shutdown ordering: host collection still only after positive stopped inspection and consumed receipt
identity and custody: uid65532, --group-add, 0o2770 roots, 0o600 manager-private, 0o660 reconstructed copy, 0o640 read-only inputs
no widening to pass: every new path refuses rather than adapts

key_inference.claim: the restrictive modes are explicitly set, not umask-derived
key_inference.consequence: a container umask would be a one-line fix and CANNOT work; checked before proposing it, not after
key_inference.why: the runtime created both permissive (0o2755 dirs, a 0o644 file) and restrictive (0o700 dir, 0o600 files) objects, which one umask cannot do since umask only removes bits; and the 0o700 directory has gid1001 with NO setgid bit, which a child of a setgid parent inherits automatically, so it was chmodded after creation

not_done: chmod or chown of either consumed tree
assuming an identity switch is already selected
not_established_and_not_assumed: whether that directory contains the selected session
whether the three 0o600 files include the session JSONL
which original collection operation failed -- the exception was collapsed to unclassified and is lost

proposal.P1a: turn 1 only; the worker relaxes exactly two objects it owns -- the one observed project directory to 0o2750 and its expected session JSONL to 0o640 -- opening O_NOFOLLOW, fstat-verifying type, uid 65532 and gid GROUP, then fchmod on that same descriptor; anything else refuses and relaxes nothing. Turn 2 relaxes nothing and the restored 0o660 manager-owned working copy is untouched.
proposal.P1b: unreadable regular file -> record closed with a new closed `content` field (read / excluded / unreadable:<errno>) and continue; unenterable directory -> REFUSE state-coverage-incomplete; unreadable selected session file -> refuse specifically. The promoted set is unchanged.
proposal.P1c: the review's closed collection step/category/errno diagnostics, unchanged

rejected_alternatives.collect as uid65532: coherent and larger; deferred not dismissed -- evidence of the symptom is not evidence this is the smallest cure, and it should be selected deliberately rather than arrived at by accident
rejected_alternatives.container umask: cannot work; umask only removes bits and the modes are explicit
rejected_alternatives.manager-side chmod of runtime state: the host granting itself access to another identity's files; excluded by PACKET and the review
rejected_alternatives.relaxing everything the runtime creates: makes the run pass and qualifies nothing

stated_limitation: if the blocking 0o700 directory is not the project directory, the correction does NOT make the run pass: P1a relaxes two named objects and P1b then refuses at state-coverage-incomplete. That is a refusal, with a named step and errno instead of unclassified -- progress, but revision 1 implied a pass and that would have been selling a guess.
verification_plan: P1a: exactly two objects change in turn 1; TURN 2 CHANGES NOTHING and a manager-owned 0o660 restored file is still 0o660 afterwards (the direct R1 regression test for D2); manager-owned, wrong-type and symlink cases each refuse through the verified descriptor; second project dir, missing UUID, nested session and credential-shaped entry refuse

P1b: unreadable non-selected file continues with content:unreadable:EACCES; unreadable selected file refuses; AN UNENTERABLE DIRECTORY CONTAINING A FOREIGN .jsonl AND A CREDENTIAL-SHAPED ENTRY REFUSES rather than reporting those absence checks as passed (the D1 regression test); .claude.json still content:excluded and never opened
P1c: eight steps under known/unknown refusal, OSError and non-OSError, with canaries in exception arguments

end to end: a synthetic runtime-owned 0o700/0o600 home fails unclassified BEFORE; AFTER, the project-directory case completes and the other-directory case refuses with a named step and errno -- both halves, because both are real
one reversal probe per new guard, isolated copies, __pycache__ removed, -B
worker_change_justification: PACKET keeps the worker unchanged unless the correction demonstrably requires it and the reason is recorded; only the owning identity may open its own objects, so P1a cannot live anywhere else
